content:
The river had been whispering secrets that night—soft, cold, and dripping with menace. I'd been trailing a lead on stolen gold bars from Swissair’s cargo hold, thought perhaps if the thief had gone too far, he’d left a piece behind. But no piece of metal turned up.

It was after midnight, a pewter sky hanging over Zurich like a bruise. I was walking along the Limmat, past the guild houses with their shuttered eyes and the river’s scum catching the last glow of streetlamps like oily sparks. Fog curled off the water, wrapping around the pilings like smoke. Then I saw it.

A coat, dark navy, caught on a rusted iron branch jutting from the bank. But it wasn’t the coat that turned my stomach—it was the arm beneath it, the hand twisted unnaturally, clutching something: a silver cigarette case, engraved with initials I didn’t recognize. The water had risen, nearly swallowing the body’s waist.

I pulled him out slow. Middle-aged, well-dressed—trousers too fine for a tramp, shoes too polished for a drinker from the docks. No ID, but his fingers bore a signet ring with a coat of arms—von Schattenstein. A name connected to old money, old grudges, and old sins that never quite dry up.

The river gave him back reluctantly, but it never forgets. And neither do I. That night, the Limmat wasn’t just water—it was a witness that didn't lie, but it also kept its secrets close, like most things in this town.
